newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada wholesale trade unchanged in Dec on month.
newsitem.headline: Canada wholesale trade unchanged in Dec on month.

text.p: Canada's wholesale trade was unchanged on a seasonally adjusted basis in December from November at C$21.72 billion, Statistics Canada said on Wednesday.
Sales, adj C$21.72 bln 0.0 pct +8.7 pct
Inventories, adj C$31.90 bln +0.5 pct +0.2 pct
Note - dollar figures are billions. Other figures are percentage changes.
StatsCan also revised its figure for November sales to C$21.73 billion from C$21.70 billion.
The agency said sales for the whole year 1996 stood at C$254 billion, 4.3 percent above the 1995 levels.
Wholesale trade represented 6.4 percent of Canada's gross domestic product in 1996, up from 5.6 percent in 1990.

In 1996, 10 out of the 11 trade groups posted increases in wholesale sales, led by the computer and packaged software industry, which gained 17.3 percent. Sales of beverage, drug and tobacco products rose 12.0 percent in the year and sales of food gained 3.8 percent.
The only group where sales declined was the "other products" group, which lost 3.2 percent in wholesale shipments.
In December, the inventory-to-sales ratio rose slightly to 1.47.
